+| LRN-6 | **Screen highlights (amended by David, 2026-10-25, feat-001).** Each element a step drives from has a red box drawn round it and a "Step n" label beside it, never a numbered circle. The step text below the screenshot names the same n. The box positions come from the app's own region tags (`data-region` and the screen contract's regions) wherever they exist, so they are measured and never placed by hand. |
 | LRN-7 | **"Check your understanding"** ends each section: a two-column table with the question on the left and the answer on the right. |
 | LRN-8 | **Comparison tables** for things that get confused, for example the test projects, the run modes and the cancellation outcomes. |
 | LRN-9 | **Code references** give a repo-relative `path:line` link and a short extract of 3 to 12 real lines, so a reader can open the code and see the idea in place. |
 | LRN-10 | **"Why" callouts** state each design decision as the choice made, the alternative and the reason. |
 | LRN-11 | **Troubleshooting:** a closing table of symptom, cause and fix, built from the problems actually met during the build: the trails' findings, and `docs/lessons.md` where it exists. |
+| LRN-12 | **Persona journeys (feat-001).** Each guide is organised as the journeys of its personas, not one section per operation: a policy servicer in the workbench, an assessor in the explorer, and a developer joining the project. Each step says what the user decides there and what Docket (or the API) gives them. |
+| LRN-13 | **Shots show the outcome (feat-001).** A step's screenshot frames the action and its result: the response, the end of the page, the plan picture. A top-of-page shot that shows no result is not a step's "what you should see". |
+| LRN-14 | **Full coverage, checked (feat-001).** A coverage map lists every feature of the guide's half (§6, §7) against the journey step that teaches it. A check script fails on any feature with no step. |

+---
+plan_id: feat-001

+---
+# feat-001: The full user guides, as persona journeys
+
+## Why
+
+The delivered guides (F7 `API_UserGuide.pdf`, F8 `UI_UserGuide.pdf`) are the 2026-10-23 short form, rushed for
+the interview. They read as a feature list with top-of-page screenshots. David, 2026-10-25:
+
+> "red circles with 1 and 2 are hard to follow we should use a red box with step label so say a text box is step
+> one the text box will have a red box drawn around it so user can clearly see where they need to drive from.
+> Most of the screenshot are just top of page - I dont see any responses shown at end of pages or plan pictures-
+> perhabs we should try to tell a story user flows and think how a user will use this and bring them on a journey
+> to learn the app how they would use it rather than sell, quote, cancel etc [...] and we need full coverage of
+> all feature- human decisions for example how do I use it how does it benefit me as a user of docket"
+
+His follow-ups the same day:
+- "Stay 1 pdf": each guide stays one PDF, with no separate start-here guide.
+- "Three personsa sounds fine as long as we have full coverage": a policy servicer in the workbench, an assessor
+  in the explorer, and a developer joining. Coverage is the condition.
+- "Split: guides move out": the guide work bug-002/N6 gave up comes here.
+
+The outcome: a reader picks up one PDF and follows a persona's journey. At each step they see the exact element
+boxed in red with its "Step n" label, and the result it produces. Every feature of that half appears on some step.
+
+Requirement lines: `docs/documentation-requirements.md` LRN-6 (amended), LRN-12, LRN-13 and LRN-14 (new), plus
+§6, §7 and §8 unchanged. These are guide requirements, not API or Docket rules, so the node has `rules: []`.
+
+## Approach
+
+### N1: Rebuild both guides as persona journeys (docs node)
+
+- **Requirements first.** The approval commit carries the LRN-6 amendment and the three new LRN rows (David's
+  words above). The builder then amends `docs/specs/guide-format.spec.md` (the red box and "Step n" label replace
+  `span.marker`), `ui-guide.spec.md` and `api-guide.spec.md` (the question bank re-grouped by persona, the
+  journey outline and the coverage map).
+- **Personas to guides** (Claude's mapping of David's three personas; change it at approval if it's wrong):
+  - `UI_UserGuide.pdf`: the policy servicer (workbench: sell, view, quote and cancel, claim, renew, inspect a
+    request, the error states) and the assessor (explorer: a rule's evidence from requirement to tests and
+    commits, a node's walkthrough, a verdict and its findings, the matrix).
+  - `API_UserGuide.pdf`: the developer joining (clone, run, the test suites by hand, where a rule lives) and the
+    servicer driving the API directly (Postman and curl, each response shown).
+- **Shots.** `docs/guides/ui/capture.mjs` re-captures from the app on `main`. It draws the red box from region
+  tags, as the markers are drawn now, and frames each step's result: the response panel, the end of the page,
+  the plan picture.
+- **Coverage check.** A new check under `docs/guides/` reads the coverage map and fails on any §6 or §7 feature
+  with no journey step. It runs beside the existing link check (`docs/guides/api/check.test.mjs`).
+- **The carried N6 work.** The API guide's launch and test sections are reprinted against `main`, with counts
+  from a run on `main`, which removes the two "not on this branch" callouts and the stale 637. `api-guide.spec.md`
+  moves to one diagram per big idea (LRN-4) and gets the four missing diagrams. F8's R6–R12 and the A2.2 note
+  are applied. Both PDFs are reprinted.
+- **Loop.** The docs sequence, with David's lighter docs loop (2026-10-23): only a P1 reopens (a command that
+  fails as printed, or a privacy leak), and a P2 becomes a PR note. The node's acceptance commands are the link
+  check, the coverage check, the privacy scan and the reprint.
+- **Out.**
+  - The matrix screen's Step 3 re-sign, routed here on 2026-10-25. It needs `/screen-resign` extended to
+    redraw a region, which is a design stage. It is deferred to its own plan, and the U1 DATA-4 test holds
+    N4's line meanwhile.
+  - Any change to `src/` or `tests/` (documentation-requirements §9).
+
+## Rejected alternatives
+
+- **Two nodes, one per guide.** Two PRs and two review rounds. The guides share the format change and the
+  capture script, so splitting them doubles the loop overhead within David's window ("2hours can be extended to
+  4-5", 2026-10-25) for no reviewable gain.
+- **Keep numbered markers and only add outcome shots.** David rejected the circles in so many words ("red circles
+  with 1 and 2 are hard to follow").
+- **A separate start-here guide per persona.** David: "Stay 1 pdf".
+- **Doing the matrix Step 3 re-sign here.** It's a screen-contract change, which is a design stage, not a docs
+  task. Putting it on the guide PR would hold the guides up behind G4-style sign-off.
+
+## Prior work consulted
+
+- `docs/plans/active/build.dag.yaml:433`: F8's acceptance, with highlight markers measured from region tags. Kept,
+  and the box replaces the marker.
+- `docs/plans/archive/bug-002.plan.md:91-99, 150-153`: the guide work N6 gave up (the "not on this branch"
+  callouts, the 637 count, one diagram per big idea, F8 R6–R12, the A2.2 note, the reprint). Carried here.
+- `docs/plans/archive/bug-002.plan.md:192`: the matrix Step 3 re-sign was routed to feat-001. It is deferred (see Out).
+- `docs/guides/ui/index.html`, `UI_UserGuide.pdf`: last changed in `5ab3eadd` (F8 A1.2/R13).
+- `docs/guides/api/index.html`, `API_UserGuide.pdf`: last changed in `64eb6808` (F7 LRN-5 green).
+- `docs/specs/guide-format.spec.md`: last changed in `fc1ee5bc`. Its `span.marker` component (`:26`) becomes the red box.
+

+### Red box and "Step n" label (LRN-6, amended)
+
+- No numbered circle, no `span.marker`. The red box is the only highlight, drawn in the guide's error red from `tokens.css`, 3 px, with no fill so the element stays readable.
+- The label reads exactly `Step n`, where n is the step's number in its journey. The step text under the shot names the same n ("Step 2: type the reference in the box"). A shot that serves several steps carries several box and label pairs, each with its own n, in step order.
+- Positions come from region tags: `capture.mjs` reads the `[data-region]` rectangle (or the element inside it that the step names) and writes percentages into the manifest. Where a tool has no region tags (Postman, Visual Studio), the box is measured from the captured pixels, never placed by eye.
+- Every `span.box` has one `span.boxlabel`, and every label's n appears in the step list beneath the same figure. The guide check fails on a box with no label, a label with no step, or an n that does not match.
+
 Lists have three items, or four at most (LRN-3); longer ones are grouped under labels.
 
+## Journeys and the coverage map (LRN-12, LRN-14)
+
+A guide is the journeys of its personas, one `section.journey` per persona, each a list of `ol.steps` steps. A step has an id of the form `<persona letter>J<n>` (for example `SJ3`), set as the `id` of its `li.step`. Each step says what the user decides (`div.decide`) and what Docket or the API gives them (`div.gives`), then shows the shot that frames its outcome (LRN-13).
+
+The coverage map lives in the guide's spec, as one fenced block with the info string `coverage`. Each non-blank line not starting with `#` is `feature-id | requirement ref | step id | feature`, split on ` | ` and trimmed. The check script (under `docs/guides/`, run beside `docs/guides/api/check.test.mjs`) fails on a feature whose step id is not a step in the guide's HTML, on a step with no feature, and on a §6 or §7 item with no line.

+++ b/docs/guides/ui/run-receipts.mjs
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+// Runs the commands the UI guide shows, on this checkout, and records each one's real output in run-output.json.
+// build.mjs copies from that file; nothing in the guide's outputs is typed by hand (documentation-requirements section 8.3).
+//
+// Usage: node docs/guides/ui/run-receipts.mjs <step>...      steps: tree trace build vitest vitest-one serve playwright playwright-one
+//        (no step runs the quick ones: tree trace build vitest vitest-one serve)
+//
+// An entry is { command, cwd, seconds, output, exit }. The checkout's absolute path is replaced by <repo> in every output
+// (the guide is public), and the time is the wall clock of the whole command.
+import { execFileSync, spawn, spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
+import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
+import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+
+const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
+const root = resolve(here, "..", "..", "..");
+const web = "src/Uinsure.Policies.Web";
+const file = join(here, "run-output.json");
+const receipts = existsSync(file) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, "utf8")) : {};
+
+const slash = (p) => p.replace(/\\/g, "/");
+const scrub = (text) => {
+  let out = text.replace(/\u001b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]/g, "").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n");
+  const forms = new Set([root, slash(root), slash(root).replace(/^([A-Za-z]):/, (_, d) => `/${d.toLowerCase()}`), slash(root).replace(/^([A-Za-z]):/, (_, d) => `/${d}`)]);
+  for (const f of forms) out = out.split(f).join("<repo>");
+  const home = slash(process.env.USERPROFILE ?? process.env.HOME ?? "");
+  if (home.length > 3) out = out.split(home).join("<home>").split(home.replace(/\//g, "\\")).join("<home>");
+  return out.trimEnd();
+};
+
+function run(name, command, cwd = ".", env = {}) {
+  const start = Date.now();
+  const r = spawnSync(command, { cwd: join(root, cwd), shell: true, encoding: "utf8", env: { ...process.env, ...env }, maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024 });
+  const seconds = Math.round((Date.now() - start) / 100) / 10;
+  receipts[name] = { command, cwd, seconds, exit: r.status, output: scrub(`${r.stdout ?? ""}${r.stderr ?? ""}`) };
+  console.log(`${name}: exit ${r.status} in ${seconds}s`);
+  save();
+}
+const save = () => writeFileSync(file, `${JSON.stringify(receipts, null, 2)}\n`);
+
+const steps = {
+  tree() {
+    // What git tracks in each folder, one line per folder: names only, so build output (dist, node_modules) never appears.
+    const dirs = [web, `${web}/app`, `${web}/app/explorer`, `${web}/app/workbench`, `${web}/kit`, `${web}/compiler`, "tests/Uinsure.Policies.Web.Tests", "tests/Uinsure.Policies.Web.Tests/e2e", "docs/ui"];
+    const lines = [];
+    for (const d of dirs) {
+      const names = execFileSync("git", ["ls-tree", "--name-only", "HEAD", `${d}/`], { cwd: root, encoding: "utf8" })
+        .trim()
+        .split("\n")
+        .map((n) => n.slice(d.length + 1));
+      lines.push(`${d}/`, `  ${names.join("  ")}`);
+    }
+    receipts.tree = { command: "git ls-tree --name-only HEAD <folder>/", cwd: ".", seconds: 0, exit: 0, output: scrub(lines.join("\n")) };
+    save();
+  },
+  trace: () => run("trace", `npm --prefix ${web} run trace`),
+  build: () => run("build", `npm --prefix ${web} run build`),
+  vitest: () => run("vitest", `npm --prefix ${web} run test`),
+  "vitest-one": () => run("vitestOne", "npx vitest run --config vite.config.ts wb-7-requests-drawer", web),
+  playwright: () => run("playwright", `npm --prefix ${web} run e2e`),
+  "playwright-one": () => run("playwrightOne", 'npx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts W1/wb-1 -g "WB-1"', web),
+  async serve() {
+    // The API's http profile (5080) and the static preview (4170) with /api proxied to it, then a status check of each.
+    const lines = [];
+    const start = Date.now();
+    const api = spawn("dotnet", ["run", "--project", "src/Uinsure.Policies.Api", "--launch-profile", "http"], { cwd: root, shell: false });
+    const preview = spawn("npm", ["--prefix", web, "run", "preview", "--", "--port", "4170", "--strictPort"], { cwd: root, shell: true, env: { ...process.env, DOCKET_API_PORT: "5080" } });
+    const seen = { api: "", preview: "" };
+    api.stdout.on("data", (d) => (seen.api += d));
+    preview.stdout.on("data", (d) => (seen.preview += d));
+    const until = async (probe, ms) => {
+      for (let t = 0; t < ms / 500; t++) {
+        if (await probe().catch(() => false)) return true;
+        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500));
+      }
+      return false;
+    };
+    await until(async () => (await fetch("http://localhost:5080/health/live")).status === 200, 120000);
+    await until(async () => (await fetch("http://localhost:4170/")).status === 200, 60000);
+    const status = async (url) => (await fetch(url).then((r) => r.status, () => "no answer"));
+    const checks = [
+      ["curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" http://localhost:4170/", await status("http://localhost:4170/")],
+      ["curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" http://localhost:5080/health/live", await status("http://localhost:5080/health/live")],
+      ["curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" http://localhost:4170/api/health/live", await status("http://localhost:4170/api/health/live")],
+    ];
+    const kill = (p) => spawnSync("taskkill", ["/PID", String(p.pid), "/T", "/F"], { encoding: "utf8" });
+    kill(api);
+    kill(preview);
+    lines.push(...checks.map(([, code]) => String(code)));
+    receipts.serve = {
+      command: "dotnet run --project src/Uinsure.Policies.Api --launch-profile http, then DOCKET_API_PORT=5080 npm --prefix src/Uinsure.Policies.Web run preview -- --port 4170",
+      cwd: ".",
+      seconds: Math.round((Date.now() - start) / 100) / 10,
+      exit: 0,
+      apiOutput: scrub(seen.api),
+      previewOutput: scrub(seen.preview),
+      checks: checks.map(([command, code]) => ({ command, output: String(code) })),
+      output: scrub(lines.join("\n")),
+    };
+    save();
+    console.log(`serve: ${lines.join(" ")}`);
+  },
+};
+
+const wanted = process.argv.slice(2);
+const todo = wanted.length ? wanted : ["tree", "trace", "build", "vitest", "vitest-one", "serve"];
+for (const s of todo) {
+  if (!(s in steps)) {
+    console.error(`Unknown step ${s}. Steps: ${Object.keys(steps).join(" ")}`);
+    process.exit(2);
+  }
+  await steps[s]();
+}

 <section class="front">
   <h2>The big ideas</h2>
   <ol>
-    <li><strong>Rules have IDs.</strong> Every rule in the brief has an ID (SELL-2, CANCEL-1b) in <code>docs/requirements.md</code>. The same ID is a test trait, a code comment and the <code>ruleId</code> in an error body.</li>
-    <li><strong>Terms.</strong> A policy is a list of terms. A renewal appends the next term and never overwrites dates, so a cancellation made in the last 30 days still works.</li>
-    <li><strong>One clock.</strong> "Today" is the UK date, computed once from an injected <code>TimeProvider</code> in Europe/London. The domain only ever receives a <code>DateOnly</code>.</li>
-    <li><strong>One error shape.</strong> Every failure is an RFC 9457 problem body. A 400, 404 or 409 is returned alone. A 422 lists every broken rule.</li>
-    <li><strong>One rounding.</strong> Money is rounded in one method, <code>Money.Round</code>: 2 decimal places, half away from zero.</li>
-    <li><strong>Prove it.</strong> 637 tests in four projects and a Postman collection of 253 requests, all green on this branch. Each rule has a unit test and an HTTP test.</li>
-    <li><strong>Evidence, not deployment.</strong> The Bicep and the Azure DevOps pipeline were built and checked locally and never deployed.</li>
+    <li><strong>A policy has a life.</strong> It is sold, is pending or active, can be renewed in its last 30 days, and ends cancelled or expired. Its status is worked out from today and never stored.</li>
+    <li><strong>Four projects, one direction.</strong> The domain holds every rule and needs only .NET. Services orchestrate, Persistence stores, the Api speaks HTTP. Architecture tests enforce who may reference whom.</li>
+    <li><strong>One pipeline.</strong> Every request passes the same stages, from forwarded headers to the repository. One injected clock decides "today", and one method rounds money.</li>
+    <li><strong>Errors come in order.</strong> A 400, 404 or 409 is returned alone. Only then are all the 422 rules checked together. Every failure is one RFC 9457 body that names the rule.</li>
+    <li><strong>A cancellation is a decision.</strong> Five outcomes decide the refund, and the response names the one that applied in <code>ruleApplied</code>.</li>
+    <li><strong>Each test proves something different.</strong> Domain, Services, Api, Architecture, the web suites and Postman each catch a different kind of mistake. Every rule ID is a test trait.</li>
+    <li><strong>Test first, shipped as evidence.</strong> Outside-in TDD built it and left a trail. The Bicep and the pipeline were built and checked locally and never deployed.</li>
   </ol>

+# QA script: feat-001 / N1, the two user guides as persona journeys, followed against the running app
+
+Rule IDs: none. N1 is a docs node (`rules: []`), so the Rule column carries `—` and names the guide step instead.
+The contract is the acceptance list for N1 in `docs/plans/active/feat-001.dag.yaml`. This script tests line 7:
+*a reader follows one persona journey in a PDF against the running app and reaches each step's shown result*.
+It also gives a light check of lines 2 and 3 (each step says what you decide and what you get back, and the shot or
+output shows the result).
+Branch: feature/feat-001/N1   Worktree: .claude/worktrees/feat-001-N1
+Commit under test: 35954f1d or later. The guides and both PDFs last changed in 11872be5. This script's own commit
+changes only this file. Record the SHA you test in the sign-off.
+API URL: http://localhost:5080 (the `http` launch profile: Development, SQLite file)   App URL: http://localhost:4170
+Run from: the worktree root, `.claude/worktrees/feat-001-N1` under the main checkout. Use Git Bash for every command.
+The guides are written for a POSIX shell.
+
+You follow four short journeys, one per persona. Each one is a subset of the guide steps, so it fits in about
+30 minutes in all:
+
+| Journey | Persona | PDF (or its HTML) | Guide steps followed | Time |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| A | Developer joining | `API_UserGuide.pdf` (`docs/guides/api/index.html`) | DJ2, DJ4, DJ6 | ~7 min |
+| B | Servicer, API | `API_UserGuide.pdf` | SJ1 to SJ6 | ~8 min |
+| C | Servicer, workbench | `UI_UserGuide.pdf` (`docs/guides/ui/index.html`) | SJ1 to SJ7 | ~10 min |
+| D | Assessor, explorer | `UI_UserGuide.pdf` | AJ1 to AJ5 | ~5 min |
+
+Run them in this order. A starts the API, B and C use it, and C starts the app that D uses.
+
+The Actual and Pass/Fail columns are empty. I didn't run the journeys (note 1). I ran
+`dotnet test --solution Uinsure.Policies.slnx` at 35954f1d (652 passed, 0 failed) and the CANCEL-1b trait filter
